subject.title: Native Slack token rotation support (oauth.v2.access refresh flow)

question: Should Slack token rotation become a built-in Slack plugin feature, and where should Slack refresh/client credentials live?
rationale: The request is useful and aligned, but it adds new sensitive config/state, OAuth refresh ownership, and live runtime credential adoption that need maintainer product and security intent before code can safely choose a permanent shape.

options.title: Build Slack-owned token rotation
options.body: Add a Slack plugin feature with SecretRef-compatible credential storage, doctor/docs/tests, and explicit proof for Socket Mode, HTTP mode, refresh failure, and live adoption.

options.title: Keep external rotation for now
options.body: Document the supported external daemon/manual rotation path and improve reload/status guidance without adding native OAuth credential ownership yet.

options.title: Design generic credential refresh first
options.body: Pause Slack-specific implementation until maintainers define a broader channel/provider credential refresh API that Slack can consume.

recommendation.title: Build Slack-owned token rotation
recommendation.body: Add a Slack plugin feature with SecretRef-compatible credential storage, doctor/docs/tests, and explicit proof for Socket Mode, HTTP mode, refresh failure, and live adoption.

likelyOwner.reason: The Slack provider/runtime history is the strongest available ownership signal for deciding whether this belongs in the Slack plugin and how it should integrate with existing Slack modes.
